title: The only number that tells the operator when the Referee can speak divides by a 437-day span containing a 212-day recording hole, and never says so
hypothesis: GET /research/desk/referee/registry/shortlist serves each starter candidate's `accrual_rate_sessions_per_day` = n_sessions / _corpus_session_span_days(newest_by_date) and `projected_days_to_target` = 12 / that rate, and /desk renders both as bare 'Accrual / day' and 'Projected days' columns beside the Select button; the denominator is the corpus's whole calendar span including every day nothing was recorded, so serving an `accrual_basis` block (first/last session date, span days, recorded + pooled session counts, the longest zero-session stretch) plus a per-candidate projection expressed in RECORDED sessions -- the unit accrual actually counts -- makes the operator's one irreversible decision readable without changing, re-tuning, or replacing a single shipped number.

evidence.measured: 2026-08-15, read-only over the operator's own store (apps/backend/.data/playbook, 210 record files; newest-per-date = 156 session dates, 2025-06-03..2026-08-13; ALL 156 at ONE detector basis 02bebbe17e7b8769 with config_fingerprint 08e471b10130e1e2, so zero stale-basis dates and numerator/denominator agree today). _corpus_session_span_days therefore serves 437 as every candidate's denominator, and 212 of those 437 calendar days are ONE stretch with no recorded session at all (2025-06-04..2026-01-01 -- the corpus holds exactly one 2025 date). Re-running the shipped formula by hand: S-1 capitulation:long 71 sessions -> 0.1625/day -> 74 projected days; S-2 jbe:long 44 -> 0.1007 -> 119; S-3 double_top:short 105 -> 0.2403 -> 50; S-4/S-5 range_trade:long at_wall ~53 sessions (playbook-band-context-v3 cache, 181 at_wall occurrences) -> ~0.121 -> ~99; S-6 range_trade:short at_wall ~66 (270 occurrences) -> ~0.151 -> ~79. Per RECORDED session -- the unit _hypothesis_accrual actually counts (a post-boundary date with >=1 occurrence in the cell) -- the SAME corpus reads S-1 71/156 = 0.455 -> 26.4 further recorded sessions, S-2 42.5, S-3 17.8, and the corpus's own recent cadence is 62 recorded sessions in the trailing 90 calendar days (0.69/day, essentially every trading day), i.e. ~26 / ~43 / ~18 trading days rather than 74 / 119 / 50 (a 2.4x-4.5x overstatement of the wait). Neither the payload (referee_registry.py:1194-1221) nor the /desk columns (apps/frontend/app/desk/page.tsx:4769-4804) discloses the denominator, the span, the recorded-session count, or the gap. Zero real registrations exist today (apps/backend/.data holds no referee_registry dir), so this number is currently the ONLY input to the era's one unmade operator decision.

journey_sketch: The shortlist fold serves an accrual_basis block plus a per-candidate projection in recorded sessions, /desk renders both beside the shipped columns, and docs/referee-statistical-spec.md Sec9 records the disclosure as a read-side planning statement no statistical procedure consumes.

title: The five referee record dirs are the only append-only stores an automated lane may still write without tripping the store-scope guard
hypothesis: project-extensions/store-scope/store-scope.env's STORE_SCOPE_PROTECTED_PATHS enumerates twelve real .data store dirs and omits every referee one, so the guard that exists precisely because a replay lane once appended three real playbook records cannot see a lane that clicks Register / Compute nulls / Evaluate on /desk against the ambient backend; listing the five resolver-owned dirs and adding a test that DERIVES the expected list from the resolvers (so a future referee store cannot drift out of protection) closes it while the dirs are still empty.

evidence.measured: 2026-08-15: store-scope.env:47 protects apps/backend/.data/{playbook, playbook_runs, playbook_backscan_runs, universe, screen, screen_runs, forward, forward_runs, topup_runs, index_reconcile_runs, bars, datasets} -- and none of the five referee dirs the era added: referee_registry (referee_registry.py:206), referee_null + referee_null_runs (referee_null.py:154/164), referee_eval + referee_eval_runs (referee_adjudicate.py:246/257), each an env-var-or-sibling default of the universe dir. The guard's own header records why it exists (goal-playbook-iter-8: a replay clicked Run Backscan against the ambient :8301 backend and appended three real playbook records into stores this project forbids pruning). /desk now carries three referee WRITE controls, and referee records are strictly worse to pollute: no update/delete/supersede path exists anywhere by design, and a junk hypothesis stays in its family's BH denominator as p=1 forever. The real dirs do not exist yet (zero registrations), so listing them costs nothing now and is unrecoverable to skip later. Not promoted this cycle: it changes no user-visible surface, so it cannot carry the [NEW]-flagged walkthrough every proposed journey owes.

journey_sketch: The five referee store dirs join STORE_SCOPE_PROTECTED_PATHS and a test derives that list from the resolver functions, so a new referee store is protected on the day it is born.

title: A registered hypothesis's accrual reads 'k of 12' with no denominator, so a stalled corpus and a thin cell look identical
hypothesis: _hypothesis_accrual serves informative_post_boundary_sessions / target_sessions with is_proxy: true and no statement of how many sessions were RECORDED since the boundary, so serving the recorded-post-boundary session count (and the newest recorded session_date) beside it -- the post-registration twin of the shortlist disclosure -- lets the operator tell 'the setup is rare' from 'the desk has not refreshed in a week' without leaving the page.

evidence.measured: 2026-08-15: referee_registry.py:868-873 returns exactly {informative_post_boundary_sessions, target_sessions, is_proxy, basis_current}; the /desk registry rows render it as a k-of-12 accrual with no denominator. The corpus's newest session_date is 2026-08-13, two calendar days before this survey, and every one of the 210 records was recorded_at 2026-08-13 (a single back-scan) -- so accrual advances only while the operator keeps refreshing, and the same corpus that gives S-1 a 71/156 = 45.5% informative rate would make '3 of 12' equally consistent with three weeks of daily refreshes and with a refresh that stopped. Unobservable today (zero real registrations), which is also why it ranks below the shortlist disclosure: it becomes useful the moment a hypothesis is registered, not before.

journey_sketch: The registry fold serves recorded-post-boundary sessions and the newest recorded session date beside each hypothesis's informative-session accrual, computed once in referee_registry.py.

title: The certificate's candidate check matches when the observation's identity and the candidate's identity are BOTH unknown
hypothesis: _candidate_matches_observation returns strategy_id == candidate.get('strategy_id') and profile == candidate.get('profile'), so a journal record whose result block carries no identity (None, None) matches a candidate dict missing both keys -- a fail-OPEN shape inside a deliberately fail-closed interlock; requiring both sides to be present strings before comparing makes the filter refuse rather than match on absence.

evidence.measured: 2026-08-15: apps/backend/app/research/referee_adjudicate.py:534-550. Unreachable on today's records -- the iteration-10 evaluator's own probe showed candidate={} pools 0 observations against records that all carry real identity strings, and authorize_promotion still requires an exact match against a live scan identity -- so this is hardening, not a live defect (the iteration-10 audit recorded it as finding B1, not a violation). Ranked last for exactly that reason, and it changes no user-visible surface, so it cannot carry the [NEW]-flagged walkthrough a promoted journey owes.

journey_sketch: The strategy-candidate identity filter refuses on absent identity instead of matching unknown against unknown, with a counter-test for the both-unknown case.
